exposure: disturbed labour (total or partial uterine inertia)
cohort: The study included medical records of 107 purebred and non-pedigree queens experiencing dystocia, comprising 111 cases, treated at a university animal hospital between 2017 and 2024.
finding: Feline dystocia was associated with high kitten mortality but low queen mortality, with maternal hyperglycaemia significantly increasing the risk of kitten mortality.
mod_finding: Most queens with dystocia were surgically treated (primarily via caesarean section), while medical treatment was efficient for non-obstructive dystocia with three or fewer foetuses remaining.
